messages:
maya: Sharing a short RFC draft — proposal for quota-aware, tiered redaction that the runtime + console can coordinate on. want quick feedback on privacy/legal/ops tradeoffs.

maya: Core idea: each request gets a redaction level computed from (route policy, tenant compliance flags, current quota pressure). levels = [none, minimal, pseudonymize, full_mask]. sampling rate for retaining unmasked or minimal logs is adjusted by quota_pressure (lower quota => more pseudonymize/full_mask).

maya: example route config (pseudo-yaml):
```
route: /v1/generate
redaction_default: minimal
redaction_overrides:
  allowlist: [internal-support, canary-tenant]
  strict_routes: [compliance/financial, compliance-healthcare]
quota_pressure_metric: telemetry.quota.pressure // 0..1
sampling_strategy: "stratified-by-importance"
importance_hint_header: X-Debug-Importance
```

arjun: q: embeddings & vector outputs — do we treat those as PII? some customers may submit PII inside prompts that ends up in embeddings.

arjun: my thought: always run an embedding-scrubber that replaces vectors with stable hash pointer for stored telemetry. don't store raw vectors unless tenant explicitly opts in with contract.

Tom H: legal input: pseudonymization via HMAC is acceptable if we rotate salts and keep salt per-tenant in KMS. example: `pseudonym = HMAC_SHA256(tenant_salt, value)[:16]` store only pseudonym + provenance metadata.

Tom H: also we should keep a short audit log entry whenever we downgrade redaction (i.e., unmask) — who unmasked, reason, TTL. must be immutable and exportable for audits.

emily: ops/telemetry note: we need metrics and dashboard panels before rolling this out. minimum metrics: `redact.rate` (percent per-route by level), `unmask.request.count`, `quota.pressure` (per-pool), `pseudonymize.salt.rotate.count`.

emily: dashboards: per-route breakdown, latency impact of redaction, and a heatmap of which tenants are causing unmask spikes.

maya: UX idea for Console: show a per-route "inspect-level" slider with 3 presets (safe, debug-pseudonymize, support-unmask) + explanation. unmask must be gated by role + a one-click breakglass with audit TTL.

maya: propose default rollout: staging canary for 5% of traffic on non-prod tenants; then gradual 1% -> 10% in prod over 2 weeks while watching `unmask.request.count` and `redact.rate`.

sre-bot: deploybot: canary rollout started for `redaction-service` -> staging cluster ci/5472. link: https://ci.internal/redaction-service/5472 :rocket:

arjun: sampling fairness: please avoid naive uniform sampling. when we sample to keep full context for debugging, use stratified sampling keyed by tenant_id + request_signature so rare failure modes don't vanish.

Tom H: fallback policy suggestion: during quota spike >0.8, force `pseudonymize` for all tenant traffic except routes in `support-breakglass` allowlist. breakglass unmask must create audit_event and expire at TTL (default 1h).

emily: tests: add unit tests for scrubber rules + e2e for the rollout. local command to run scrubber against sample corpus: `./tools/scrubber --config examples/route-redact.yaml --corpus testdata/prompt-samples.json`

maya: outstanding questions: 1) embeddings retention policy (agreeing with arjun?) 2) exact pseudonym length + rotation cadence 3) console role policy wording for breakglass

maya: action items: i) arjun to draft embedding-scrubber implementation ii) Tom to coordinate legal wording & audit spec iii) emily to sketch dashboards + alert thresholds iv) me to land config + canary script.

maya: thumbs? :thumbsup: :thinking_face:

Tom H: LGTM but want legal to sign off on HMAC rotation cadence.

arjun: +1, I'll PR scrubber tomorrow and include a small benchmark for CPU cost.

emily: i'll make a minimal dashboard and add alerts for `unmask.request.count > 5/min` per-org.

sre-bot: note: staging canary finished deploy 1777770059, rollback window open til 1777770360.

maya: thanks all — will collect comments and update the draft.
